body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{RV}}\): if \(h_n\to0\), then \(\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\delta_n}(O_i)/(\sqrt n\sigma_n)\Rightarrow N(0,1)\); if \(h_n\to h_0\in(0,\infty)\), then \(a_n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\delta_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow L_{\kappa,H,h_0}\); and if \(h_n\to\infty\), then \(a_n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\delta_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow S_{\alpha,H}\). Uniformity is branchwise over compact parameter sets separated from the two transition boundaries. This is a strict multiplier-domain extension of Kennedy's fixed-compact Gaussian result because it includes diverging \(\delta_n\) and two non-Gaussian branches.
body.justification: The theorem locates the exact stochastic frontier at which a positivity-robust incremental mean acquires weak-overlap non-Gaussian uncertainty.
body.gap: Kennedy2019Incremental stops at fixed compact multipliers, while MaWang2020RobustIPW varies trimming for a fixed target and therefore has neither the moving centering nor the IPSI contrast mark.
body.consumer: It determines when the Gaussian approximation in \(\mathtt{npcausal::ipsi}\) must be replaced as analysts extend odds shifts beyond a bounded range.
